confidence_notes: I ran six web searches: one for the RBA rate and five for restaurant, coffee, beer, cocktail and wine prices. The sources were aggregated cost-of-living sites, mostly crowdsourced and inconsistent in date. These included Mylifeelsewhere, Traveltables, CityCost (updated Oct 2026), Expatistan and a Numbeo-based French site (updated Nov 2026). Restaurant meal, coffee and beer anchors are reasonably supported. Cappuccino was about €2.5-3.2, a 0.5 l domestic draught about €2.3-3.0, an inexpensive meal about €10-12, and a mid-range three-course dinner for two about €45-61. The FX figure is from the RBA exchange-rate search result, 18 Nov 2026. I converted euro prices at roughly 1.17 USD/EUR, which is an assumption. The sources were not specific to July 2026, so I added a modest tourist-season and inflation uplift. The cocktail has one direct data point (about €6-7 in a downtown club, plus a nightlife guide saying drinks run €4-9). I set it at roughly 2.4x the restaurant beer price. No reliable restaurant wine-by-the-glass price was found, only retail bottle prices of about €6.5-7 and a bar listing pours of €4-7. I estimated a glass at about €3.7 using the local relationship to beer and bottle prices. All four accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates for July peak-season Bratislava. I did not search for accommodation prices or inspect any booking pages or listings, so those are the least certain anchors.
comparable_city_reasoning: Bratislava sits between Prague/Budapest and Vienna on price. It is cheaper than Vienna on restaurants (roughly 25% lower per the comparison data) but higher than the Slovak average. Euro-zone pricing and Old Town tourist demand in July push drinks and accommodation above the national level.
